ownShare: The first finding traces to my own round-10 request. I asked for the exclusive condition to be replaced by an enumeration of the outcomes that delete the Sandbox, and the enumeration is what carries the new error: it asserts a case — a look ending with no report — whose branch neither of us read. That is the fault I named last round, committed by the correction I asked for, which is the clearest evidence I have that the remedy is reading the path rather than writing more precisely. I would not have caught it by re-reading the sentence; I caught it because the pair read `check.go` and I then read it too.

keyFindings.description: The enumeration is right about three of its four cases and wrong about the fourth. It says the Sandbox goes with the pod whenever the check pauses between looks or closes, listing 'a look that ends with no report at all' among the outcomes that take it, and makes a reported `pending` with a queued wake the only exception. An unreported look has the same exception: `checkLookEnded` calls `endLook` (`workflow/check.go:472-482`), `endLook` ends it 'as a report of pending would' and calls `endLookPending` (`:223-231`), and `endLookPending` returns through `startLook` when `check.PendingCauseKind != ""` (`:255-256`) — before the suspend and before the `IssueSuspend` enqueue at `:257-262`. So a deployment or build wake arriving during a silent look (`:378-393` populates that cause) starts the next look on the same pod. The accurate shape is that the queued wake is the exception for both a reported `pending` and a look that ends without a report. `packages/claude-envoy/legion/skills/legion-architect/SKILL.md:419-422` carries it.

`SuspendIssue`'s own contract comment still says 'a later re-admission starts only after this patch and resumes the Sandbox'. This change removed the non-releasing path — `:60` deletes the Sandbox unconditionally once the pod is gone — so there is nothing to resume, and the package's own test requires the opposite: `issue_suspend_test.go:135` fails unless re-admission comes back with a different Sandbox UID and a different pod, 'a Sandbox and pod of its own'. The sentence was true for a parked close before this change and is newly false in a file this change rewrote, so it is in scope by the same rule that excluded `production_audit` and `issue_pvcs`. The thermonuclear quality pass asked me that scope question directly before filing; this is the answer.
